display.title: Episode 415: Hashem Is Truly Everywhere (Tu B'Shvat, Shabbos Shirah)
display.summary_short: A listener answers the Mitzvah Time phone quiz and leads the Shema, the hidden meaning of 'Echad', and a story with the song 'Hashem Is Here, Hashem Is There'.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Parshas Beshalach and Tu B'Shvat 5750. Uncle Yossi explains the new Mitzvah Time phone quiz and leads the Hakochainik march. He reviews last week's lesson on the Shema, the first mitzvah in the first Mishnah of Berachos, and plays a recorded phone call in which a young listener answers every question correctly and then leads all the listeners in the Shema over the phone. After tzedakah, Mitzvah Time teaches the kavanah of the word Echad: as the Gemara explains, Hashem is the one Master of the seven heavens and the earth (the letter ches, eight) and of the four directions (the letter dalet). Story time tells of a boy whose homework is to count how many directions he can point to; his mother finds him pointing all around the playroom, and he teaches her the new song 'Hashem is here, Hashem is there, Hashem is truly everywhere.' The show closes with Tu B'Shvat, the fruits of Eretz Yisroel and their brachos, Shabbos Shirah, and candle time.
display.lesson: Hashem is truly everywhere: up, down and in every direction. Think of this when you say 'Echad' in the Shema.
